doc.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016

title: Hearing himself on 'Azure Eyes' and the influence of Tim Hagans
summary: Jenkins identifies his own record, then talks about aggressive articulation and following Tim Hagans in Kenton's band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Ah, that’s me. What is that on? Oh that’s —
I forget what record that’s on.
“Azure Eyes,” yeah. That’s the title track of that. That’s what I thought it was.

I love sort of aggressive articulation even when playing a ballad. And I think I heard that, and with Clifford too. [scats] Like you don’t have to just mumble everything even if you’re playing a ballad.
Yeah. That’s interesting. I agree with you. You know one of my influences was a guy named Tim Hagans who was on Stan Kenton’s band before me. I took his place. Tim is a © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

beautiful player and we are good friends, even though I don’t get to see him very often. But Tim is very aggressive. And those are big shoes to fill when I got on Kenton’s band. He went on to other things. And I think I got some of that aggressive articulation from him a bit. In fact there was a time when I had to kind of say, “I’ve got to stop sounding so much like Tim Hagans.” I mean he had a record come out years later and a friend of mine came up and said, “I heard a guy play and he sounds just like you.” And Tim had sent me this record and I said, “no, that’s not what’s going on there.” I said, “I sound like him.” And I was right. Yeah. He’s a great player. Tim Hagans.
